title: observability: automate prometheus/grafana/logshipping for private installs
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Automated observability stack for Private installs: Prometheus, Grafana, log shipping, dashboards, alerts, and upgrade/rollback automation. Operators can opt-in/out and customize storage, TLS, and log sinks. See docs/private/observability.md for configuration details.
description: Motivation and summary: Private customers deploying Redwood in VPC/on-prem require a repeatable, auditable observability stack that follows our hosted defaults. This PR automates Prometheus and Grafana provisioning, standardizes dashboards and alerts, and wires log shipping (Vector/Fluentd) into customer log sinks during Private installs. It aims to reduce manual post-install steps and provide safe upgrade/rollback behavior for observability components. Changes in this PR include Helm chart additions and refactors, a Terraform module to create IAM roles/network rules/S3 buckets (for log archiving) when running in cloud-backed private installs, installer hooks for migration/rollback, and documentation updates. Commit summary: 1) Add observability subchart to redwood-helm-charts with Prometheus Operator, Grafana, and alertmanager manifests and sane defaults. 2) Add values schema and example values for Private installs (tls, storage, nodeSelectors, tolerations). 3) Add terraform module redwood-private-monitoring to provision monitoring infra (with outputs used by installer). 4) Integrate terraform module into private-installer provisioning flow and add smoke checks. 5) Add Vector/fluentd chart and templates for log shipping to S3/ELK with optional sampling and parsing rules. 6) Add upgrade and rollback hooks in installer to migrate Prometheus data and safely restore dashboards on rollback. 7) Add dashboards (redwood-overview, serving-latency, kv-cache-hitrate) and alerts (high-latency, scrape-failures, disk-pressure) plus unit tests and docs. Files changed (high level): redwood-private-installer/{main.go,install.go,helm_hooks.go,docs.md}, redwood-helm-charts/observability/{Chart.yaml,values.schema.json,templates/*}, redwood-terraform/modules/private-monitoring/{main.tf,outputs.tf,vars.tf}, redwood-helm-charts/logging/{Chart.yaml,values.yaml,templates/vector.yaml}, redwood-docs/private/observability.md, examples/private/observability-values.yaml, ci/helm-lint.yaml, ci/terraform-validate.yaml. Testing and CI: Ran helm lint, terraform validate, unit tests for installer hooks, and an internal e2e smoke test against a vSphere-based private cluster. Initial CI run had one flaky e2e that timed out; retriggered and passed. All checks green at merge time. Review thread (selected): "Ravi Patel: Can we avoid cluster-level Prometheus in air-gapped installs? Suggest adding nodeSelector limits and option for namespace-scoped operator." Author reply: "Added values to opt out of cluster-wide CRDs and documented namespace-scoped mode; added nodeSelector/toleration settings." "Jordan Lee: Need rollback step to restore dashboards when downgrading stack schema." Author reply: "Added post-rollback hook to restore dashboards from backups created during upgrade; added unit tests around hooks." "Sofia Gomez: Terraform IAM role needs least-privilege justification." Author reply: "Documented required permissions and added variables to scope role to monitoring resources only." Security and compliance: KMS key usage added as optional variable for remote S3 encryption in terraform module; docs updated with recommended configuration for regulated customers. Upgrade/rollback notes: Installer will perform a dry-run of Helm upgrades for observability charts, snapshot Prometheus data (when using persistent storage) before applying migrations, and create a dashboard backup in S3 (or cluster Secret) prior to upgrade. Rollback path restores dashboards and re-applies previous chart values. Operators can opt-out of automatic data snapshotting and backups via values. Rollout plan: This is gated behind a feature flag in the installer and only enabled for new installs by default; for existing installs operator must opt-in via installer CLI or console. Observability defaults aim to match hosted metrics (metric names, label conventions) to simplify alert parity. Known limitations and follow-ups: 1) Initial implementation assumes cluster has sufficient persistent volume class; will add automated PVC probing in a follow-up (ENG-4920). 2) Metrics cardinality tuning for very high-traffic customers will be iterated after rollout. 3) On fully air-gapped installs without an S3-compatible sink, vector will write to local PVC and operator must handle off-cluster shipping. Documentation: Updated redwood-docs/private/observability.md with configuration examples, troubleshooting, and CSP-specific notes. Examples: examples/private/observability-values.yaml included for common cloud and vSphere patterns. Merge and deployment: PR was squashed and merged into release/2.3 after approvals from reviewers and SRE sign-off. Post-merge actions: updated helm chart index, published terraform module version v1.0.0 in the private registry, and bumped installer default feature flag to enabled for new private installs. CI checks attached: see ci_checks field. Overall impact: reduces manual setup time for customers, standardizes alerts/dashboards across deployments, and provides safe upgrade/rollback behavior for observability components in Private installations.
